title: Bed making to the hotel standard
audience: Cleaners on short-stay, hotel-style and serviced-apartment turnovers who make beds for guests.
learningOutcomes: Build a bed in a fixed sequence of layers so that it looks the same each time.
Check each layer for stains, tears, lint and hair before the bed is accepted.
Handle clean linen so that it stays clean from the store to the bed.

instruction.heading: Scope, and the link to the linen handling lesson
instruction.body: Used linen handling, sorting, laundering and amenities are covered in “Linen handling, bed preparation and guest amenities”. Read that lesson before this one. This lesson covers the bed itself: how it is built, how it looks, and the checks made before it is accepted. The first stage of the room sequence removes the linen, which is when the mattress, protector and base are seen for stains and damage. Those checks are made at that point and are part of this lesson's standard.

instruction.heading: Building the bed in layers
instruction.body: Build the bed in a fixed order so that it looks the same every time. Fit the mattress protector flat and smooth, with no creases across the top. Place the bottom sheet and square the corners, tucking the sheet so it is smooth on the mattress. Add the top sheet with its decorative edge in the set position, and fold it at the head of the bed as the property's standard requires. Place the blanket or duvet, then the bedspread or throw. Set the pillows last, with the open side facing away from the door. Smooth each layer before the next one goes on, because creases trapped under a later layer are hard to remove.

instruction.heading: Clean hands and clean linen
instruction.body: Handle clean linen only with clean hands, and keep it off the floor. Do not drag linen across the room. Carry it against the body, away from bins and from any bathroom area. Do not place clean linen on the bathroom floor, on a bin, or on any surface that has not yet been finished. Wash or sanitise hands, or change gloves, after handling rubbish or cleaning products and before touching clean linen.

instruction.heading: Checking the bed before you leave it
instruction.body: Stand at the foot of the bed and look at it from the door side, as a guest would first see it. Check that each layer is square and that nothing hangs unevenly. Look for hairs, crumbs and lint. Press the top of the bed to check it is firm and free of lumps. Check each pillow before placing it, and reject any cover that is stained, torn or thin. If a cover is stained, torn or thin and there is no spare in the room, do not use it. Report it under the spare linen procedure.

procedure: Confirm the bed linen set for the room from the property's list, and check that each item is clean and undamaged.
Check the mattress, the mattress protector and the base for stains, tears and damage. Report anything found.
Fit the mattress protector flat and smooth.
Make the bottom sheet, the top sheet, the blanket or duvet and the bedspread in order, smoothing each layer as you go.
Place the pillows in the set arrangement, checking each cover first.
Check the bed from the door side for square lines, lint, hair and firmness.
Report any linen that is stained, torn or below standard, and follow the spare linen procedure.

workedExamples.situation: A king bed in a short-stay apartment. The mattress protector has a small stain near the foot. A spare protector is in the linen store.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can you leave the stained protector in place because the sheets cover it?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The standard covers what is on the bed, and a stain under the sheets can be felt or seen when the bed is turned down. Replace the protector from spare stock, bag the stained one as “Linen handling, bed preparation and guest amenities” sets out, and report the stain so that it is recorded.

equipmentAndPpe: Clean linen from the property's set
Spare linen from the business's stock for replacements
Clean hands, and gloves where the product or task requires them

commonErrors.error: Leaving a stained protector in place because the top sheet hides it.
commonErrors.prevention: Check every layer, including the protector, for stains, tears and damage.

commonErrors.error: Dragging a sheet along the floor on the way to the bed.
commonErrors.prevention: Carry linen off the floor and keep it clear of bins and bathroom areas.

commonErrors.error: Making the bed with hands that have just handled rubbish or the bathroom.
commonErrors.prevention: Wash or sanitise hands, or change gloves, before touching clean linen.

commonErrors.error: Placing pillows without checking the covers.
commonErrors.prevention: Check each pillow cover before it goes on the bed.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Used linen is handled as “Linen handling, bed preparation and guest amenities” sets out, including checks for sharps and contamination. Do not shake linen.
Lift a mattress with a safe technique, use a second person, or leave the lift to a team member if it is too heavy to lift safely alone.

qualityStandard: Each layer is square and smooth, with no creases across the top of the bed.
Protector, sheets and covers are free of stains, tears and visible hair or lint.
Clean linen is never placed on the floor or on an unfinished surface before the bed is made.
documentationEvidence: Linen check recorded on the room checklist
Report of any stained, torn or missing linen, with the room number
summary: Build the bed in the same layers each time, and smooth each layer before adding the next.
Check the mattress, protector, sheets and covers for stains, tears and lint.
Keep clean linen clean by using clean hands and keeping it off the floor and away from bathroom work.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is the mattress protector checked when the bed is first stripped?
options: Because stains under the sheets are still part of the room standard
Because protectors are not included in the room standard
Because the protector is only checked when a guest complains

knowledgeChecks.question: A top sheet has a small stain, and there is no spare in the room. What is correct?
options: Use it after a quick rinse, because a small stain is not a hygiene risk
Do not use it; report it and get a replacement under the spare linen procedure
Turn it over so that the stain is at the foot of the bed

knowledgeChecks.question: Which practice keeps clean linen clean?
options: Dragging it across the floor to the bed, since the floor is clean
Holding it in the crook of the arm while wiping the bin
Handling it only with clean hands and keeping it off the floor
